articles.summary: Ardent Health Announces Definitive Agreement to Acquire Boone Health wroberts Thu, 11/12/2026 - 16:42 Provides $200 million capital commitment over 10 years to expand access and services, invest in facilities and technology, and recruit physicians to Mid-Missouri BRENTWOOD, Tenn. and COLUMBIA, Mo. (Nov. 12, 2026) – Ardent Health (NYSE: ARDT), a leading provider of healthcare in growing mid-sized urban communities across the U.S., today announced a definitive agreement to acquire Boone Health , a not-for-profit health system based in Columbia, Missouri, for a purchase price of $47 million in cash. The acquisition will include the 392-bed Boone Hospital Center, Boone Health Medical Group, 19 sites of care, related ancillary services and associated real estate. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to customary closing conditions. Boone Health has served patients across Columbia and Mid-Missouri for more than 100 years and has operated as an independent system since 2021, building a strong reputation for clinical quality and patient care. In 2025, the Boone Health Board of Trustees and Board of Directors announced a search for a strategic partner that could provide additional capital and resources to support the system's continued growth. Ardent was selected after a comprehensive evaluation process led by an independent advisory firm. "Boone Health has built an outstanding reputation for quality, nursing excellence, patient care and outcomes, and we are honored its Board of Trustees and Board of Directors selected Ardent as its partner for the future," said Dave Caspers, president and chief executive officer of Ardent Health. "This agreement advances our disciplined capital allocation strategy and provides a significant opportunity to expand patient access, strengthen specialty services and invest in care delivery. We are committed to investing in Boone Health’s facilities, technology and people so the organization can continue delivering high-quality healthcare to residents of Columbia and the 26 counties of Mid-Missouri for generations to come." “Boone Health has been a cornerstone of care in Columbia and Mid-Missouri for more than a century,” said Jerry Kennett, MD, chair of the Boone Health Board of Trustees. “In Ardent, we identified a partner that supports our mission, respects our culture and can accelerate our vision without compromising what makes Boone Health special. Following a thoughtful review, the Board is confident Ardent is the right long-term partner for Boone Health. This agreement protects what our community has built while giving Boone Health the resources it needs to grow." Key commitments under the agreement include: A $200 million capital commitment over 10 years to fund equipment, facility renovations, new facilities and services, physician recruitment and information systems, with emergency department expansion and operating room modernization among the near-term priorities. A commitment to maintain Boone Health's essential hospital services with a focus on strengthening its role as a regional referral center. Continued employment for all active Boone Health employees, physicians and advanced practice providers in good standing. Establishment of a local advisory board for Boone Hospital Center , ensuring Columbia and Mid-Missouri stakeholders have an ongoing role in the hospital's operations. Continuation of Boone Hospital’s existing charity care policy. Together, these commitments are designed to help Boone Health build on its strong foundation while positioning the system for its next chapter of growth. They also reflect Ardent’s strong history of investing in the communities it serves. Beyond capital, Ardent brings systemwide quality and safety programs, technology and IT infrastructure, physician recruiting support, and operating expertise that can help Boone Health strengthen specialty services, expand access and support local care teams. Since 2003, Ardent has invested over $2 billion in its hospitals and health systems to strengthen care and improve outcomes. Ardent facilities consistently achieve high performance across clinical and safety measures, exceeding national benchmarks on key quality indicators including sepsis care, hospital-acquired infections and serious safety events. "Ardent's track record of investing in community-based health systems, maintaining strong quality and expanding access aligned with our long-term vision for this organization,” said Brady Dubois, chief executive officer of Boone Health. “This partnership will allow us to build on our strengths, invest in new services and continue delivering the high-quality care our community has come to expect from Boone Health." Ardent and Boone Health will continue to operate as separate organizations until the transaction closes, with no immediate changes to patient care, employee roles or day-to-day operations. About Ardent Health Ardent Health (NYSE: ARDT) is a leading provider of healthcare in growing mid-sized urban communities across the U.S. The Company delivers care through its subsidiaries, which include 30 acute care hospitals and more than 280 sites of care with over 2,000 employed and affiliated providers across six states. Anchored by a shared operating model and a commitment to investing in innovative services and technologies that improve quality, access and experience, Ardent is focused on delivering strong clinical outcomes and improving the health of the patients and communities it serves. About Boone Health Boone Health is a locally governed, not-for-profit health system based in Columbia, Missouri, serving patients across 26 Mid-Missouri counties. It is anchored by Boone Hospital Center, a 392-bed regional referral hospital, along with physician clinics, outpatient services and other care sites. With strengths in cardiology, neurology, oncology, orthopedics, surgical and obstetrical services, Boone Health employs more than 2,000 staff and 350 physicians on its medical staff. Boone Hospital has consistently been ranked by outside organizations as the top hospital in the region for patient quality and outcomes, and one of the top hospitals in the state recommended by patients. Test case generation now appears in products from Tricentis, BrowserStack, Qase, TestRail, and most other test management vendors, and several add assistants that summarize runs or suggest which tests to execute. For enterprise QA teams, though, the question is no longer whether a test management platform has AI. That distinction separates a generic chatbot bolted onto a test repository from a test management platform where AI is part of the QA workflow. For enterprise buyers, the difference shows up in the quality of generated tests, in how much review effort AI output needs, and in whether InfoSec approves the rollout.

articles.summary: 3D Systems Celebrates 40 Years During Formnext 2026 Kara Caldwell Thu, 11/12/2026 - 16:32 Release Date Thursday, Nov 12, 2026 4:30 PM The inventor of 3D printing to highlight the history and the future of 3D printing at key industry trade show Recognition for the early innovators across the industry who helped build the additive industry Visit booth D11 in Hall 11 at Formnext to see new developments in MultiJet 3D printing, Direct Metal 3D printing and more. ROCK HILL, South Carolina, November 12, 2026 – 3D Systems (NYSE:DDD) today announced plans to celebrate, at Formnext 2026, the 40th anniversary of the founding of 3D Systems and 43 years of the invention of SLA 3D printing by co-founder Chuck Hull. With guest appearances by Chuck Hull and opportunities to see and touch the original 3D-printed part, attendees can understand the origins of additive manufacturing, combined with 3D Systems’ vision of the future of manufacturing. “The 3D printing industry has grown steadily to more than $16B at the end of 2025 after more than 40 years of existence in large part thanks to Chuck Hull and 3D Systems,” said Scott Dunham, Executive Vice President of Research at Additive Manufacturing Research . “Chuck's dedication to this industry, and in turn 3D Systems' ongoing development of many foundational technologies, is commendable. Our projections for additive manufacturing estimate an industry of at least $65B by 2035, which is incredible when put into the context of beginning from one man's idea for a rapid prototyping technology.” While Chuck Hull has always been very humble about his own invention of SLA, he has also been admiring of innovations that came after, either via 3D Systems or from other inventors who have been either partners or competitors to 3D Systems, all of whom helped build the industry to where it is now. “This is a true celebration for 3D Systems, but also the 3D printing industry as a whole,” said Chuck Hull, inventor of 3D printing, CTO and co-founder of 3D Systems. “Turning this small idea into a $16 billion industry has been the result of hard work and a drive to succeed by many in the industry. The drive of entrepreneurship and innovation by everyone is what has made this industry grow and we want to celebrate that.” The Emergence of Competition in 3D Printing Following the commercialization of SLA, other key inventors emerged with different approaches to solving additive manufacturing. Scott Crump invented and patented Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) 3D printing in 1988, and with his wife, Lisa Crump, co-founded Stratasys (NASDAQ: SSYS). Stratasys provided an alternative to SLA 3D printing and rapid prototyping, helping to develop and expand the industry alongside 3D Systems. “We are excited to join Chuck Hull in this celebration of the 3D printing industry,” said Scott Crump, co-founder and Board Member of Stratasys. “Watching it grow from a series of bright ideas into a vital additive manufacturing industry has been incredibly fulfilling. None of it would have been possible without the passion and drive of pioneers like Chuck Hull and the many others who have helped make the industry what it is today.” In the 1980s, Carl R. Deckard, an undergraduate student at The University of Texas at Austin, conceived the idea for Selective Laser Sintering (SLS), a process that uses a laser to fuse powdered material into solid objects. He continued developing the idea through his master’s and doctoral studies under Dr. Joseph Beaman, his professor and mentor. Beaman recognized Carl’s talent and gave him the support, technical guidance, and freedom to explore that helped turn his idea into a working manufacturing process. DTM was acquired by 3D Systems in 2001. “Carl came up with a wild idea of making parts as he watched Star Trek one night and thought about the special effects of using sand as a backdrop when ‘beaming down’ to the planet. We worked on the idea and brought it to Joe who helped him make it work. It took quite a bit of dedication from both of them to get SLS out of the lab and into the market,” said David K. Leigh, a fellow student and colleague of Deckard’s. “DTM Corporation licensed the technology from UT Austin and developed it for commercial use. Carl died in 2019 at just 58. We lost him too soon, but the work he and Joe did together continues to make a difference today.” Another influential figure from the industry’s origins is Joe Allison, who joined 3D Systems in 1987 and filed 12 patents for the company across 3 years. He later formed Solid Concepts, which quickly became one of the world’s largest suppliers of 3D printed parts. Allison is now CEO of Gentle Giant Studios, a leading 3D printing and digital art company involved in the movie business. “Chuck Hull not only invented a technology but he founded an industry that has profoundly changed the way things are manufactured,” said Allison. “3D printing has repeatedly proven itself as the way forward for highly complex parts where the limitations of traditional manufacturing have been a barrier. We will see the industry continue to grow and develop in ways that no one can predict.” There are yet more inventors who have been and continue to be key influencers in the industry and so acknowledgement also goes to individuals including: Max Lebovsky, CEO, Formlabs; Andy Christensen, founder of Medical Modeling; Yoav Zeif, CEO, Stratasys; Emanuel Sachs who first invented binder jetting 3D printing; and many many more. From the History to the Future of 3D Printing Across the last 4 decades, the 3D printing industry has seen periods of growth and decline, optimism and doubt, but through the belief and innovation of many in the industry, it has grown far beyond what many would have expected. Chuck Hull continues to inspire new innovations in the industry. “3D printing continues to strengthen because of the inventiveness of people in applying it, perfecting the materials and processes,” said Dr. Jeff Graves, President & CEO, 3D Systems. “We have entered an era where 3D printing is now enabling unheard-of performance in space, automotive, dental and medical fields. With 3D printing, the sky is not the limit.” Attendees at Formnext will be able to hear Chuck Hull present alongside Patrick Dunne, SVP, Advanced Applications, 3D Systems, at 3.45 pm on Tuesday November 17, 2026 on the Technology Stage, Stand #B49 in Hall 12.1. You can join 3D Systems in celebrating both the last 40 years and the future of 3D printing at Formnext between 5 – 8 pm, Booth D11 in Hall 11, November 18 2026, Frankfurt, Germany About 3D Systems For 40 years Chuck Hull’s curiosity and desire to improve the way products were designed and manufactured gave birth to 3D printing, 3D Systems, and the additive manufacturing industry. Since then, that same spark continues to ignite the 3D Systems team as we work side-by-side with our customers to change the way industries innovate. As a full-service solutions partner, we deliver industry-leading 3D printing technologies, materials and software to high-value markets such as medical and dental; aerospace, space and defense; transportation and motorsports; data center infrastructure; and durable goods. Each application-specific solution is powered by the expertise and passion of our employees who endeavor to achieve our shared goal of Transforming Manufacturing for a Better Future. articles.summary: The Short Version In short: don’t switch on automated dunning until four checks pass on every invoice. Here are the numbers behind that call. A 2022 survey found 85% of finance and business services leaders said poor communication directly caused customers not to pay invoices. About 35% of finance leaders name communication quality as a major obstacle in collections. Automated dunning amplifies existing process flaws. A bad-data reminder can reach a large portion of your customers every billing cycle. Reminders sent against wrong invoices, unapplied payments, or open disputes create friction and manual work instead of collecting cash. Payment matching breaks for ordinary reasons: missing reference numbers, partial payments, consolidated transfers, short-pays, bank fees, or incorrectly posted credits. The four pre-automation checks are invoice accuracy, payment application status, dispute escalation rules, and dunning cadence measured against customer contact history. A due date passing should trigger verification of the invoice amount, payment application, and dispute status before any message sends. Don’t Scale Dunning Until Your AR Data Passes A reminder built on flawed AR data doesn’t just miss. It hands the customer a reason to doubt your billing operation and hands your collections team one more exception to untangle.
